title: Semisimple Lie algebra
statement:
A finite-dimensional Lie algebra in characteristic zero is
*semisimple* if it has no nonzero solvable ideal (in the sense of
[def-wf-lie-algebra]).

mathlib_searches.query: A semisimple Lie algebra has no nonzero solvable ideals
A Lie algebra has trivial radical if and only if every solvable Lie ideal is zero

mathlib_match.how: Specializes in one line: for the given characteristic-zero field k and finite-dimensional Lie algebra L, use HasTrivialRadical k L (Defs.lean:64-65) as the predicate called semisimple in this blueprint. The theorem hasTrivialRadical_iff_no_solvable_ideals k L (Basic.lean:67-69, hypotheses at line 51) says exactly HasTrivialRadical k L iff every ideal I with IsSolvable I equals bottom, i.e. there is no nonzero solvable ideal. The theorem requires only CommRing k, LieRing L and LieAlgebra k L; no additional hypotheses or comparison argument is needed. The same LieIdeal and IsSolvable notions are already recorded by def-wf-lie-algebra. This does not identify the definition with Mathlib IsSemisimple, whose direct-sum definition is different.

It says HasTrivialRadical ↔ every solvable LieIdeal is ⊥, which is exactly the blueprint definition, including I = L and with no Nontrivial assumption. The how field rightly does not identify the item with IsSemisimple (direct sum of atoms, Defs.lean:105).
